runner.note: This is the only runner in the repository that executes a conformance directory, and it executes the wrong one. evals/fixtures/protocol-conformance.json records normative_owner as conformance/vibeproof/v1/exact-byte-vectors.json and then runs conformance/protocol/vibeproof-v1-vectors.json, an unsigned eleven-field shadow codec whose authority_class is exploratory-prototype and whose evidence_ceiling is cross-language-parity. The normative corpus has never been executed by anything. That substitution is exactly the condition a per-suite manifest exists to make visible, and it stays open under PF-001.

cases.title: Agree byte-for-byte across Rust and Go on the shadow codec vector
cases.note: Cross-language agreement on a prototype codec. Under the harness contract's own rule this can never be conformance, because both subjects consume a corpus the normative owner does not own.

negative_case_gap.reason: The corpus is an exploratory shadow codec that should not be normative at all. Adding rejecting vectors to it would deepen the substitution rather than repair it; the repair is quarantining the shadow protocol and executing conformance/vibeproof/v1/ instead.

note: The suite holds one fixture and no negative case, so it cannot show that either subject rejects anything. Recorded rather than repaired: the repair is quarantining the shadow protocol under PF-001, not adding rejecting vectors to a corpus that should not be normative in the first place.
